name: Pricing Table
hint: Answer the strip above the cards. The plan that fits takes the lead and its badge travels to it.
description: The plan cards section of a pricing page, set in Stint (time tracking and invoicing for freelancers and small studios): Starter, Pro, Studio and Enterprise, monthly or yearly, in three currencies. It helps you choose instead of just listing prices. A "What do you need?" strip (a team-size stepper plus invoices, client portal and SSO switches) picks the cheapest plan that fits, and that card takes the lead: one measured frame and its "Recommended for you" badge spring from the old card to the new one while the card lifts, its CTA turns primary and a notch under the strip slides across to point at it. Inside every card the lines you asked for light up, and what a plan can't do appears crossed out with where to find it ("On Studio and up", "Your team is 12"). Prices roll digit by digit on billing, currency and team-size changes, including the per-seat maths ("$20 × 4 seats = $80 a month"). The answers are optional; until one is given the default recommendation stands. Sized by its container: four cards in a row when wide, three with Enterprise as a slim row on the stage, and on a phone a snap rail with the lead centred, a plan index and a sticky summary of the card in the middle. Reduced motion keeps every highlight and swaps the travel for a fade.
intents: pricing cards section that recommends a plan
plan tiers with a monthly and yearly toggle
recommend the right plan from a few questions
saas pricing table with recommended plan badge
pricing tiers with rolling prices and a currency switch
usage: Use as the pricing section of a marketing page, above Plan Comparison Table (point the Compare link at it). Three or four tiers in price order plus an optional custom plan (price: null) work best; tag each feature line that answers a chooser question with its `need` id so cards can highlight it or explain where it lives. Keep needs to two or three switches that actually separate the plans. For a single seat-slider card use Odometer Pricing instead; for every line item use Plan Comparison Table. The small line above the heading is `eyebrow` (text) with `logo` (a node) before it: pass your own mark, `logo={null}` for text only, or `eyebrow=""` with `logo={null}` to drop the line. It shows only what you pass: no `plans` means no cards and no chooser, and `demo` fills the blanks with a made-up product called Stint. Pass your own `heading`, `plans`, `needs`, `currencies`, `lede`, `links`, `finePrint` and `recommended`. Pass `onSelect` to act on a plan button (it gets one object, `{ plan, billing, currency, seats, item }`: `plan` is the plan's id and `item` the plan object); the buttons do nothing else. Set `loadingPlan` to that plan's id while checkout starts and clear it after. Prices print through `formatPrice(amount, { currency, symbol })` when the currency symbol before the number is not right for you, and the fixed words through `labels`. `simulate` fakes a working-then-done cycle on them for demos (the gallery turns it on) and is off by default, so leave it off in real UI. A page that also shows Plan Comparison Table should hold one billing state: pass `billing` and `onBillingChange` to both (or give the comparison `showBilling={false}`), and `onCurrencyChange` here feeds the comparison's `currency`. Prices print the same way in both: whole amounts bare, anything else to the cent ($7.20). The badge text (`badgeDefault` / `badgeFit`) is reused in the phone summary bar, so one plan carries one label; match Plan Comparison's `recommendedLabel` to it.

dataProps.description: The billing period, controlled when passed with `onBillingChange`. Passed alone (the older use) it sets the switch and follows the prop when it changes, and the reader can still flip it.
The currency code, controlled when passed with `onCurrencyChange`. Passed alone it sets the switch and follows the prop.
Text of the small line above the heading. Empty by default; `demo` shows the sample's.
The mark before the eyebrow, about 13px, drawn in the accent chip. None by default (`demo` shows the sample mark); pass your own node.

[{ id, name, blurb, price, priceUnit?, priceLabel?, note?, seats: { max?, label }, features: [text | { text, need }], cta }]. price: 0 = free, null = custom (shows priceLabel), or a per-seat price: { CODE: [monthly, yearly] }, [monthly, yearly], or one number for both. Empty by default: no plans, no cards and no chooser.
Chooser switches: [{ id, label, noun, phrase, icon }]. Feature lines point at them with `need`. Empty by default.
[{ code, symbol }]. The symbol is printed before amounts unless you pass `formatPrice`. Two or more show a currency switch. Empty by default (amounts print bare).
Links under the cards: [{ label, href, icon?, onClick? }]. In-page #anchors scroll smoothly. Empty by default.
Paragraph under the heading. Empty by default.
Small print under the cards. Empty by default.
Title of the chooser strip.
Hint under the chooser title.
Badge on the `recommended` plan before any answer, and its tag in the phone summary bar.
Badge once the chooser has picked a plan.
Starting team size.
Largest team the stepper allows.
Heading level of the section title.

({ plan, billing, currency, seats, item }) => void when a plan button is pressed. `plan` is the plan id, `item` the plan object you passed, `billing` "annual" or "monthly", `currency` the code, and `seats` the team size once the reader has set one (otherwise undefined). Not called while `disabled` or while `loadingPlan` is set.

(billing: "annual" | "monthly") => void when the reader flips the billing switch. With `billing` it makes the switch controlled: hold it in page state and pass the same value to Plan Comparison Table.
(code) => void when the reader picks a currency. With `currency` it makes the switch controlled; pass the same value on as Plan Comparison Table's `currency`.

(amount: number, { currency, symbol }) => string. Prints every amount (card prices, the struck-out monthly price, the per-seat maths, screen-reader text). Default: the currency's symbol, then the number with whole amounts bare and others to the cent.

Replaces the fixed words: { billingPeriod, monthly, annual, save: (n) => string, currency, unit ("per seat / month", used when a plan has no priceUnit), billedMonthly, teamSize, person, people, weNeed, clear, plans, more, custom }. Pass only the keys you change.
Id of the plan whose checkout is running: its button shows a spinner and no plan button fires until you set it back to null.
The root <section>.

example:
<PricingTable
  eyebrow="Relay pricing"
  logo={<RelayMark />}   // or logo={null}
  heading="One price per person"
  lede="Start free, upgrade when the team grows."
  recommended="team"
  plans={[
    { id: "free", name: "Free", blurb: "For trying it out.", price: 0, priceUnit: "forever", seats: { max: 3, label: "Up to 3 people" }, features: ["One shared inbox"], cta: "Start free" },
    { id: "team", name: "Team", blurb: "For growing teams.", price: { USD: [9, 7.2] }, seats: { max: 50, label: "Up to 50 people" }, features: [{ text: "Automations", need: "automations" }], cta: "Start a trial" },
  ]}
  needs={[{ id: "automations", label: "Automations", noun: "Automations", phrase: "automations", icon: "zap" }]}
  currencies={[{ code: "USD", symbol: "$" }]}
  links={[]}
  finePrint="Prices exclude tax."
  billing={billing}
  onBillingChange={setBilling}
  formatPrice={(n, { currency }) => new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "currency", currency, maximumFractionDigits: n % 1 ? 2 : 0 }).format(n)}
  loadingPlan={checkingOut}
  onSelect={({ plan, billing }) => startCheckout(plan, billing)}
/>
